In the year 2000, colleges and universities represented critical institutions in the global
higher education landscape. The sector experienced significant transition, characterized by
growing enrollment rates, evolving academic structures, and the emergence of new
institutional frameworks. This documentation provides a comprehensive overview of
college systems, structures, and characteristics during this pivotal period in educational
history[1][2]. The year 2000 marked a turning point in global higher education. Sixty-three percent of the
high school graduating class of 2000 in the United States enrolled in colleges or universities
in the fall, reflecting widespread access to higher education[1]. Gender disparities remained
evident, with college enrollment rates for young women at 66.2 percent compared to 59.9
percent for young men[1]. Higher education institutions worldwide were experiencing unprecedented growth in
student numbers. Key enrollment patterns included:
Undergraduate dominance: Approximately 89% of total enrollment consisted of
undergraduate students[2]
Postgraduate enrollment: About 9% of students pursued postgraduate
qualifications[2]
Doctoral enrollment: Only 0.65% of total enrollment pursued doctorate degrees[2]
Racial and ethnic diversity: Among high school graduates, white students showed
higher college enrollment (64.0%) compared to black (56.2%) and Hispanic (53.0%)
graduates[1]
Universities in 2000 operated through clearly defined academic structures. The typical
university comprised multiple colleges and departments, organized hierarchically for
administrative and instructional purposes. College Documentation 2000

The year 2000 represented a transitional moment in higher education. Colleges worldwide
were experiencing growth in enrollment and diversification of programs, while
simultaneously confronting challenges of quality, access, and equity[1][2]. The institutional
structures, governance systems, and academic frameworks established during this period
would form the foundation for significant changes in the following decades.
